title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 10: Agan v. Piatco — Validity of a BOT Contract
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 10: CJP's account of Agan v. Piatco, voiding the NAIA Terminal III contracts under the Build-Operate-Transfer law
sub_topics: The facts: AEDC's unsolicited proposal (1993) and Piatco's award for NAIA Terminal III
The five challenged agreements (concession plus supplements)
Grounds of invalidity: prequalification, right to match, delay, one-sided terms
The BOT Law (RA 6957) and the public interest

stances.claim: The NAIA Terminal III concession agreements were void for grave irregularities and one-sided terms contrary to law and public interest.

notable_anecdotes: Six business leaders formed AEDC in 1993 and submitted the original unsolicited proposal.
decision_framework_signals: void-for-illegality plus public-interest test on BOT contracts
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 10 recounts Agan v. Piatco, one of the most publicized cases of CJP's eighth year, which voided the agreements for the NAIA Terminal III airport project. He narrates the facts — AEDC's 1993 unsolicited proposal, Piatco's award, and the five challenged agreements — and the grounds of invalidity (questionable prequalification, denial of the right to match, delay, and one-sided terms) under the Build-Operate-Transfer Law (RA 6957).
